title: Conference-matrix MDS code conjecture
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, and let ${\mathbb C}$ be a code of length $p+1$ constructed from a generator matrix that is a conference matrix. **Conference-matrix MDS conjecture.** The code ${\mathbb C}$ is an MDS code of dimension $\frac{p+1}{2}$ and minimum Hamming distance $\frac{p+3}{2}$. This would give an MDS code with parameters determined by the rank of a conference matrix over ${\mathbb Z}_p$; the source provides no resolution of the claim.
source_name: Tuvi Etzion, Alexander Vardy and Eitan Yaakobi, “Coding for the Lee and Manhattan Metrics with Weighing Matrices”, arXiv:1210.5725 (2012).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.5725

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2012).

title: Concavity conjecture for the generalized inverse hyperbolic sine
statement:
For $x\in(0,1)$ fixed, let $p\mapsto {\rm arcsinh}_p(x)$ denote the generalized inverse hyperbolic sine as a function of $p$. **Concavity conjecture.** The function $p\mapsto {\rm arcsinh}_p(x)$ is strictly concave on $(0,\infty)$. In particular, for all $p>1$ and $x\in(0,1)$,

$$
{\rm arcsinh}_p^2(x)>{\rm arcsinh}_{p-1}(x){\rm arcsinh}_{p+1}(x).
$$

This conjecture is motivated by computer experiments; the asserted strict concavity would imply the displayed Turán-type inequality.
source_name: Árpád Baricz, Barkat Ali Bhayo and Matti Vuorinen, “Turán type inequalities for generalized inverse trigonometric functions”, arXiv:1305.0938 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0938

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

title: The spectral characterization of geodesic growth for right-angled Coxeter groups on trees
statement: Let $T$ and $T'$ be trees. Assume that they are simultaneously co-spectral, their complements are co-spectral, and their line graphs are co-spectral. **Geodesic-growth conjecture.** Then $T$ and $T'$ have the same geodesic growth, meaning that the associated right-angled Coxeter groups $G(T)$ and $G(T')$ have the same geodesic growth series. The conjecture asks whether these three spectral data determine geodesic growth for right-angled Coxeter groups based on trees; the paper establishes examples supporting the question but does not resolve the general implication.
source_name: Laura Ciobanu and Alexander Kolpakov, “Geodesic growth of right-angled Coxeter groups based on trees”, arXiv:1504.02774 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.02774

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

title: Starlikeness conjecture for Cassinian balls in starlike domains
statement: Let $G\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain that is starlike with respect to $x\in G$, and let $B_{c_G}(x,r)$ denote the Cassinian ball of radius $r$. **Starlikeness conjecture.** For every $r>0$, the ball $B_{c_G}(x,r)$ is starlike with respect to $x$. This is a proposed extension of convexity results to starlike domains, and the paper does not establish it.
source_name: Riku Klén, Manas Ranjan Mohapatra and Swadesh Kumar Sahoo, “Geometric properties of the Cassinian metric”, arXiv:1511.01298 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.01298

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

title: The combinatorial injection conjecture for dominance order on compositions
statement:
Let $A,a,B,b$ be integers with $A \geq B \geq 0$ and $a \geq b \geq 0$. For $m,n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{U}^m_n$ denote the set of compositions of $n$ with $m$ non-negative parts. For compositions $\lambda$ and $\mu$, write $\lambda\mu$ for their concatenation, and write $\trianglerighteq$ for the dominance order induced by the non-increasing rearrangements. **Combinatorial injection conjecture.** There is an injection

$$
\gamma: \mathcal{U}^A_b \times \mathcal{U}^B_a \hookrightarrow \mathcal{U}^A_a \times \mathcal{U}^B_b
$$

such that, for every $(\lambda_1,\mu_1) \in \mathcal{U}^A_b \times \mathcal{U}^B_a$, if $(\lambda_2,\mu_2)=\gamma((\lambda_1,\mu_1))$, then

$$
\lambda_1\mu_1 \trianglerighteq \lambda_2\mu_2.
$$

This conjecture gives a combinatorial formulation implying the case $k=2$ of the paper's theorem relating total nonnegativity of the matrices $\mathcal{T}_p$ and $\mathcal{S}_p$.
source_name: Clifford Smyth, “A Probabilistic Characterization of the Dominance Order on Partitions”, arXiv:1512.04084 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.04084

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

title: A fully supported local information maximum on the full two-shift
statement: Let $(X,T)$ be the full two-shift, let $\alpha$ be the partition used to define information, and consider the space of one-step Markov measures on $X$. A measure is fully supported when every allowed cylinder has positive measure, and a local maximum is understood relative to this space. **Fully supported local-maximum conjecture.** There is a fully supported one-step Markov measure that is a local maximum of $\operatorname{Int}_\mu(X,T,\alpha)$ among all one-step Markov measures. The assertion is suggested by numerical computations in the source; no proof or resolution is supplied.
source_name: Karl Petersen, “Measuring Complexity in Cantor Dynamics”, arXiv:1607.02425 (2016).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1512.01143](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01143).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.02425

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

title: The expressivity hierarchy conjecture for finitely iterated supervenience languages
statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^n}$ be the propositional language with the $n$-ary supervenience operator $\Rrightarrow^n$.

**Expressivity hierarchy conjecture.** For all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^{n+1}}$ is more expressive than $\mathcal{L}_{\Rrightarrow^n}$.

The paper establishes the corresponding result for $n=0$ and leaves the generalization to future work.
source_name: Jie Fan, “A Modal Logic of Supervenience”, arXiv:1611.04740 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.04740

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2016). “Recall that $\mathbb{LS}$ has been established in Sec. and shown to be sound with respect to the class of all frames.”

title: Odd-coordinate kernel conjecture for singular io-decomposable Riordan graphs
statement:
Let $G_n(g,zg)$ be a singular io-decomposable Riordan graph, let ${\cal A}_n$ be its adjacency matrix, and let $X=[x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n]^T$ be an eigenvector with eigenvalue $0$. Define the odd-index and even-index subvectors by

$$
X_o=[x_1,x_3,\ldots,x_{2\lceil n/2\rceil-1}]^T,
$$

$$
X_e=[x_2,x_4,\ldots,x_{2\lfloor n/2\rfloor}]^T.
$$

**Odd-coordinate kernel conjecture.** Then

$$
X_o=O_{\lceil n/2\rceil}.
$$

This claim is motivated by Sage computations and, together with the preceding block-matrix lemma, would constrain the zero-eigenspace of every singular io-decomposable Riordan graph. No proof or resolution is supplied.
source_name: Gi-Sang Cheon, Ji-Hwan Jung, Sergey Kitaev and Seyed Ahmad Mojallal, “Riordan graphs II: Spectral properties”, arXiv:1801.07021 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.07021

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

title: Conjecture on recurrent component cardinalities in sinkless rotor networks
statement:
Let $C_n$ be the bidirected cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i}$ denote the unique recurrent component of level $m$ and weight $i\in\mathbb{Z}_n$. Write $r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i})$ for the number of recurrent configurations in this component.

**Recurrent-component cardinality conjecture.** For $n\geq 3$, $m\geq 1$, and $i,j\in\mathbb{Z}_n$, one has

$$
r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,i})=r(\mathcal{C}_{n,m,j})
$$

whenever

$$
\gcd(n,m,i)=\gcd(n,m,j).
$$

The conjecture refines the observed near equality of recurrent-component sizes in sinkless rotor networks on bidirected cycles. It is supported by data for small values of $m$ and $n$, but the supplied source does not state a resolution.
source_name: Swee Hong Chan and Lionel Levine, “Abelian networks IV. Dynamics of nonhalting networks”, arXiv:1804.03322 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.03322

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

title: The 2-adic valuation conjecture for even-colored 2-ary partition functions
statement:
Let $c_m(n)$ denote the $m$-colored binary partition function, and let $
u_2$ be the 2-adic valuation. For positive integers $k,n$ and nonnegative integers $k$ as specified below, consider the differences of the values of $c_m$. **2-adic valuation conjecture.** For $kin\mathbb{N}_{+}$ and each $n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{2k}(4n)-c_{2k}(n))=\nu_{2}(n)+2\nu_{2}(k)+3.
$$
 Moreover, for $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{4k+1}(4n)-c_{4k+1}(n))\geq\nu_{2}(n)+3,
$$
 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{4k+3}(4n)-c_{4k+3}(n))\geq\nu_{2}(n)+6.
$$
 In each case, equality holds for infinitely many $n\in\mathbb{N}$. These predictions are motivated by known sharp congruences for the ordinary binary partition function and numerical computations for $m\leq10$ and $n\leq10^5$; their general validity remains open.
source_name: Maciej Ulas and Błażej Żmija, “On p-adic valuations of certain m colored p-ary partition functions”, arXiv:1904.03398 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.03398

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

title: The edge-pattern convex-combination conjecture
statement:
Let $P$ be a $d$-regular edge-rooted pattern of depth $r$ and girth $2r+2$. For each edge-rooted pattern, let $\mathbf{e}(P)$ denote its constraint vector, and let $\mathcal{T}'_r(d)$ be the specified family of $d$-regular edge-rooted trees of depth $r$. The constraint $\mathbf{e}(P)$ is **weaker** than a convex combination of constraints from this family in the sense that there exist $T_1,\dots,T_m\in\mathcal{T}'_r(d)$ and $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\in[0,1]$ with

$$
\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1
$$

and, for every $\bm{\alpha}\in{\left(\mathbb{Q}^+\right)}^{r+1}$,

$$
\bm{\alpha}^{\!\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\mathbf{e}(T_i)\right)\ge 1\quad\implies\quad\bm{\alpha}^{\!\top}\mathbf{e}(P)\ge 1.
$$

This would explain why the bounds obtained from edge-rooted trees remain valid at girth $2r+2$, and would generalize the cases checked for $r=2$ and $d\in\{3,4\}$.
source_name: François Pirot and Jean-Sébastien Sereni, “Fractional chromatic number, maximum degree and girth”, arXiv:1904.05618 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.05618

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

title: Equitable partitions of rectangular grid graphs
statement:
Let $P_m\oblong P_n$ be the rectangular grid graph, and let its automorphism group act naturally on its vertices. An equitable partition is a partition in which every vertex in a cell has the same number of neighbors in each cell.

**Grid-graph equitable-partition conjecture.** The equitable partitions of $P_m\oblong P_n$ are the orbit partitions of natural actions of the subgroups of the automorphism group of the graph. The lattice of equitable partitions is isomorphic to the lattice of subgroups exactly when there is a vertex with trivial stabilizer subgroup. This happens unless $2\le m=n\le3$.

The claim concerns the relationship between equitable partitions and symmetry-induced orbit partitions for rectangular grid graphs. The supplied text reports this as an apparent pattern based on computations, but gives no resolution or proof.
source_name: John M. Neuberger, Nandor Sieben and James W. Swift, “Invariant synchrony subspaces of sets of matrices”, arXiv:1908.05797 (2020).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1807.10954](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.10954).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.05797

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

title: The growth constant for the stack-sorting map
statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $s:S_n\to S_n$ be the stack-sorting map, and let $\deg(s:S_n\to S_n)$ denote its maximum fiber size. The paper considers the exponential growth rate

$$
\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\deg(s:S_n\to S_n)^{1/n}.
$$

**Stack-sorting growth conjecture.** The value of this limit lies in the interval $(1.68,1.73)$.

The interval is suggested by computations on random permutations for $n=100$ and $n=300$. The problem of obtaining improved asymptotic estimates, or exact formulas, remains open.
source_name: Colin Defant and James Propp, “Quantifying Noninvertibility in Discrete Dynamical Systems”, arXiv:2002.07144 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.07144

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

title: The rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ and $\overline{G}$ be nontrivial connected graphs of order $n\geq 8$. Write $rvd(G)$ for the rainbow vertex-disconnection number of $G$. **Rainbow vertex-disconnection Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture.**

$$
rvd(G)+rvd(\overline{G})\geq n.
$$

This conjecture proposes an improvement of the established lower bound for the sum of the rainbow vertex-disconnection numbers of a graph and its complement. The paper notes that the bound holds when $rvd(G)=1$, but does not establish it for all nontrivial connected graphs of order at least $8$.
source_name: Xueliang Li and Yindi Weng, “Further results on the rainbow vertex-disconnection of graphs”, arXiv:2004.06285 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.06285

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2020).

title: Latin-strategy characterization conjecture for the symmetric group
statement:
Let $\mathbb{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements. A **Latin strategy** is obtained by choosing an $n\times n$ Latin square $S$; Alice's message identifies a row of $S$ that agrees with the input permutation at the maximum possible number of positions. An optimal strategy is one attaining the maximum success probability.

**Latin-strategy characterization conjecture.** Optimal strategies are exactly Latin strategies.

This conjecture proposes a complete characterization of optimal strategies, extending the explicitly described shift strategies. The paper states it as an open question and does not prove the characterization.
source_name: Artur Czumaj, George Kontogeorgiou and Mike Paterson, “Haystack Hunting Hints and Locker Room Communication”, arXiv:2008.11448 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.11448

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

title: Estrada–Mugnolo's Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture for hubs-biased resistance distances
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Write $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-repelling resistance distance, $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)$ for the standard Kirchhoff index, and $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-attracting resistance distance.

**Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture.** For $\alpha\in\{-1,1\}$,

$$
\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G),
$$

with equality if and only if $G$ is regular.

The conjecture was formulated after computational experiments on more than 12,000 connected graphs with $5\leq n\leq 8$, and predicts that hubs-repelling navigation gives the largest Kirchhoff index while hubs-attracting navigation gives the smallest. Its general validity is left open in the source.
source_name: Ernesto Estrada and Delio Mugnolo, “Hubs-biased resistance distances on graphs and networks”, arXiv:2101.07103 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07103

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

title: Circulant graph conjecture for monophonic position number two
statement: Let $n$ be an integer, and let a **circulant graph** mean a graph whose vertices are arranged cyclically with adjacency determined by a fixed set of cyclic differences. The monophonic position number is denoted by $a$, and the diameter by $D$. **Circulant graph conjecture.** For any $n\geq 11$, there is a circulant graph with order $n$, monophonic position number $a=2$, and diameter $D=2$. The preceding theorem establishes existence of some graph with these parameters if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5,8\}$ or $n\geq 11$; the conjecture strengthens the large-order existence assertion by requiring the graph to be circulant, based on computational evidence.
source_name: James Tuite, Elias John Thomas and Ullas Chandran S. V., “On some extremal position problems for graphs”, arXiv:2106.06827 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.06827

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

title: Subgraph criterion for minimal doubled 3-regular graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a doubled 3-regular graph. Perform the YY-$\Delta$ transformation on all wyes in all possible ways to obtain a graph $G'$ of smallest size. A **chain of 3-cycles** is a chain of one or more 3-cycles, each connected by a vertex that is also doubly adjacent to one more vertex, with the 3-cycles at either end having one vertex with exactly 4 neighbours and no connections of size greater than 2.

**Minimality criterion conjecture.** The graph $G'$ is a minimal graph if and only if it does not contain such a chain of 3-cycles.

The conjecture proposes that, for doubled 3-regular graphs, checking the more restricted subgraphs illustrated in the first column of the paper's figure suffices to determine minimality. The source gives examples and discusses related reducible subgraphs, but provides no proof or resolution.
source_name: Shannon Jeffries and Karen Yeats, “A degree preserving delta wye transformation with applications to 6-regular graphs and Feynman periods”, arXiv:2110.07764 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

title: Unit-gap conjecture for diameters of Schrijver graphs
statement:
Let $k$ and $r$ be integers with $2\leq r\leq k-2$, and let $D(G)$ denote the diameter of a graph $G$. For $n=2k+r$, write $\operatorname{SG}(n,k)$ for the Schrijver graph. **Unit-gap conjecture.** If $2\leq r\leq k-2$, then

$$
D\left(\operatorname{SG}(2k+r,k)\right)-D\left(\operatorname{SG}(2k+r+1,k)\right)\in\\{0,1\\}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the possibility of larger drops in the diameter as $r$ increases. It is based on computations and is open; the paper notes that the analogous differences are in $\\{0,1\\}$ for $k\leq 5$, while a larger gap occurs at the transition from $r=1$ to $r=2$ when $k\geq 6$.
source_name: Agustina Victoria Ledezma, Adrián Pastine, Pablo Torres and Mario Valencia-Pabon, “On the diameter of Schrijver graphs”, arXiv:2112.01884 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.01884

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

title: Uniqueness conjecture for power domination reconfiguration graphs of complete bipartite graphs
statement: Let $K_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with part sizes $s$ and $t$, and let $\mathscr{PD}^{TAR}(K_{s,t})$ denote its power domination reconfiguration graph under token addition/removal reconfiguration. **Uniqueness conjecture.** $\mathscr{PD}^{TAR}(K_{s,t})$ is unique if and only if $s\ne 2$ and $t\ne 2$. This is supported by the uniqueness results for $K_{1,t}$ with $t\ge 3$ and $K_{3,3}$, together with Sage computations for $s\in\{3,4\}$ and $t\in\{3,4,5\}$; the conjecture proposes the complete characterization, including the cases not covered by those results.
source_name: Beth Bjorkman, Chassidy Bozeman, Daniela Ferrero, Mary Flagg, Cheryl Grood, Leslie Hogben, Bonnie Jacob and Carolyn Reinhart, “Power domination reconfiguration”, arXiv:2201.01798 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01798

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

title: Even-arity complete full tree local antimagic chromatic number conjecture
statement:
Let $T$ be a complete full $t$-ary tree, meaning a rooted tree in which every nonleaf has exactly $t$ children and all leaves have the same depth. Let $l$ be the number of leaves and let $\chi_{la}(T)$ be the local antimagic chromatic number. **Even-arity complete full tree conjecture.** For every even integer $t\geq2$,

$$
\chi_{la}(T)=l+1.
$$

The paper explicitly states this conjecture as open; it would sharpen the established upper bound $\chi_{la}(T)\leq l+2$, while the equality is proved in the paper for odd $t$.
source_name: Martin Bača, Andrea Semaničová-Feňovčíková, Ruei-Ting Lai and Tao-Ming Wang, “On local antimagic vertex coloring for complete full t-ary trees”, arXiv:2204.04479 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.04479

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

title: Improved upper bounds for Staller–Maker–Breaker domination numbers
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with minimum degree $\delta(G)$. The S-game and D-game parameters are denoted by $\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)$ and $\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)$, respectively.

**Improved SMBD-number bounds.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{(i) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)\le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil-\delta(G)+1;\\
&\text{(ii) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)\le \left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor-\delta(G)+1.
\end{aligned}
$$

These bounds would improve the known sharp general upper bounds when the minimum degree is at least two; the authors note that sharp examples under this degree condition are not known.
source_name: Csilla Bujtás and Pakanun Dokyeesun, “Fast winning strategies for Staller in the Maker-Breaker domination game”, arXiv:2206.12812 (2022).
references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2107.10805](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10805), [arXiv:2106.01166](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.01166), [arXiv:1606.01317](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01317), [arXiv:1503.07891](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.07891), [arXiv:0906.4142](https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.4142).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12812

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

title: Strict middle-graph increase conjecture for outer-connected domination
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\ge 2$. The **strict middle-graph increase conjecture** asserts that

$$
\gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(G) < \gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(M(G)).
$$

The paper notes that this inequality holds for trees and for several standard graph families, including complete graphs, wheels, friendship graphs, complete bipartite graphs, and cycles. Whether it holds for every graph of order at least two remains open.
source_name: Farshad Kazemnejad, Behnaz Pahlavsay, Elisa Palezzato and Michele Torielli, “Connected and outer-connected domination number of middle graphs”, arXiv:2206.15439 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15439

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

title: Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture for generalized Paley graphs
statement: Let $d>1$ be an integer. Let $q \equiv 1 \pmod {2d}$ be a power of a prime $p$, and let $r$ be the largest integer such that $d \mid \frac{q-1}{p^r-1}$. The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ is a clique in the generalized Paley graph $GP(q,d)=\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{F}_q^+;(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^d)$. **Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture.** The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ forms a maximal clique in $GP(q,d)$. This conjecture asserts that the largest subfield producing a subfield clique cannot be extended to a larger clique. The paper resolves it in a stronger form under a sufficient-size hypothesis, while the unrestricted statement is the conjecture being addressed.
source_name: Chi Hoi Yip, “Maximality of subfields as cliques in Cayley graphs over finite fields”, arXiv:2209.00864 (2022).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2106.01522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.01522).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00864

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2022). “In , Yip described a similar phenomenon in Peisert graphs and conjectured that $\F_q$ forms a maximal clique in a Peisert graph with order $q^4$ provided that $q>3$; this was confirmed by Asgarli and Yip in .”

title: The prime-modulus conjecture for progression-free digit sets
statement:
Let $p\geq 13$ be a prime with $p\equiv 1\bmod 4$, and let $n$ be an integer divisible by $(p+3)/2$. For a digit set $D\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_p$, write $S(D,n)$ for the set of vectors in $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ in which every digit of $D$ occurs the same number of times. Define

$$
D=\left\{0,1,\ldots,\frac{p-1}{2},\frac{p+3}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Prime-modulus progression-free-set conjecture.** The set $S(D,n)$ does not contain any arithmetic progression of length $4$.

This conjecture extends the progression-free constructions for odd progression lengths to a case not covered by the stated theorem, motivated by computations with small primes. Its status is unresolved in the source.
source_name: Christian Elsholtz, Benjamin Klahn and Gabriel F. Lipnik, “Large Subsets of Z_m^n without Arithmetic Progressions”, arXiv:2211.02588 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.02588

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

title: Linear-bound multiset reconstruction conjecture for tableau minors
statement: Let $k\geq 1$ and let $T\in\operatorname{YT}(n)$, where $n\geq k+4$. Here $\operatorname{mM}_k(T)$ denotes the multiset of $k$-minors of the standard Young tableau $T$. **Multiset reconstruction conjecture.** The multiset $\operatorname{mM}_k(T)$ determines $T$. This proposed linear bound is supported by computer verification for $k\leq 5$, and concerns reconstructibility from multisets of $k$-minors.
source_name: William Q. Erickson, Daniel Herden, Jonathan Meddaugh, Mark R. Sepanski, Cordell Hammon, Jasmin Mohn and Indalecio Ruiz-Bolanos, “Young tableau reconstruction via minors”, arXiv:2307.13161 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13161

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

title: The set-palette conjecture for complete graphs
statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. In a general edge-coloring of $K_n$, let $\tau_s(n)$ denote the minimum number of colors needed so that all triangles have distinct color palettes when a palette is viewed as the set of colors appearing on its three edges. **Set-palette conjecture.** For $n\geq4$,

$$
\tau_s(n)=n-1.
$$

The source notes the inequality $\tau_m(n)\leq\tau_s(n)\leq\tau'(n)$ and states that this conjecture would imply the preceding multiset-palette conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Monika Pilsniak and Mariusz Wozniak, “A note on edge colorings distinguishing all triangles in a graph”, arXiv:2407.19050 (2024).
references:

title: Largest rigid facet conjecture for Vietoris–Rips complexes of hypercubes
statement:
Let $Q_n=\\{\pm1\\}^n$ be the Hamming cube with Hamming distance. A subset is **maximally diameter-$r$** if its diameter is $r$ and adjoining any point outside it produces diameter greater than $r$; it is **rigid** if every point has a point at distance equal to the diameter. Let $b'(n;r)$ be the size of the largest maximally diameter-$r$, rigid subset of $Q_n$, equivalently the largest such rigid facet in $\operatorname{\mathcal{VR}}(Q_n;r)$. **Largest rigid facet conjecture.**

$$
b'(n;r)=2^r
$$

whenever $n\geq r$. The subcube $Q_r\times\\{\mathbf 1_{n-r}\\}$ supplies an extremal candidate of size $2^r$, but the conjectured upper bound is not proved in the source.
source_name: Joseph Briggs, Ziqin Feng and Chris Wells, “Facets in the Vietoris–Rips complexes of hypercubes”, arXiv:2408.01288 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.01288

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

title: Contact-order distance conjecture for colored graph representations
statement: Let $G$ be a graph whose vertices are colored with $z$ and $w$, and let $i$ be a vertex from which the representation is computed. The **contact order** is the order describing how the associated level curves approach one another near a boundary singularity. **Contact-order distance conjecture.** The contact order of the representation computed from vertex $i$ is twice the path distance from $i$ to the closest vertex colored $w$. The source reports computational evidence for this extension, but does not state a proof or resolution.
source_name: Lily Adlin, Giovani Thai, Samuel Tiscareno and Ryan Tully-Doyle, “Cauchy Transforms of Colored Graphs in Two Variables”, arXiv:2410.10695 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10695

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

title: The local antimagic chromatic number conjecture for joins of matching and null graphs
statement:
Let $r,s\ge 1$ and $m\ge 2$. For a graph $G$, its **local antimagic chromatic number** $\chi_{la}(G)$ is the least number of distinct induced vertex labels among bijective local antimagic edge labelings of $G$. Let $(2s+1)P_2$ be the disjoint union of $2s+1$ copies of the two-vertex path, let $O_m$ be the null graph on $m$ vertices, let $\vee$ denote the graph join, and let $2r((2s+1)P_2\vee O_m)$ be the disjoint union of $2r$ copies of this join.

**Local antimagic chromatic number conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{la}\bigl(2r((2s+1)P_2\vee O_m)\bigr)=3.
$$

This is posed as an open problem in the conclusion, extending results on local antimagic chromatic numbers for joins of special graph families. The claim predicts a constant value of $3$ throughout the stated parameter range.
source_name: Gee-Choon Lau and Wai Chee Shiu, “On local antimagic chromatic number of the join of two special families of graphs – II”, arXiv:2410.17674 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17674

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

title: Maximum sigma_t-irregularity conjecture for connected triangle-free graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices. Write $sigma_t(G)$ for its $sigma_t$-irregularity. Among such graphs, the extremal complete bipartite graphs are conjectured to have maximum $sigma_t(G)$.

**Triangle-free extremal conjecture.** Among connected triangle-free graphs on $n$ vertices, the extremal complete bipartite graphs have the maximum $sigma_t(G)$-irregularity.

The paper proves the corresponding extremal result among complete bipartite graphs and proposes this conjecture as the extension to all connected triangle-free graphs; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Slobodan Filipovski, Darko Dimitrov, Martin Knor and Riste Škrekovski, “Some results on σ_t-irregularity”, arXiv:2411.04881 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04881

title: Nonexistence conjecture for cubic 8-circulant nut graphs
statement: A **cubic $8$-circulant nut graph** is a cubic nut graph admitting an $8$-circulant structure. **Nonexistence conjecture for cubic $8$-circulant nut graphs.** There exists no cubic $8$-circulant nut graph. This is the only unresolved case in the cubic $\ell$-circulant nut graph existence problem; computational results suggest that such graphs might not exist, but no proof is given here.
source_name: Nino Bašić and Ivan Damnjanović, “On cubic polycirculant nut graphs”, arXiv:2411.16904 (2024).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1808.08747](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.08747).

title: The majorization characterization conjecture for ordinal spaces embeddable in the line
statement:
Let $(X,\delta)$ be an ordinal space with $|X|=n\in\mathbb N^+$, and let $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ be an enumeration of its points satisfying the majorization property. Write $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^1$ for embeddability of $X$ in the real line. **Majorization characterization conjecture.** If such an enumeration exists, then

$$
X\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^1.
$$

The paper proves that line embeddability implies the existence of an enumeration with the majorization property and states sufficiency for $n\leqslant4$, while explicitly saying that it cannot determine whether sufficiency holds for $n>5$; the general assertion is therefore open.
source_name: Karsten Keller and Evgeniy Petrov, “Ordinal spaces”, arXiv:2412.17391 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.17391

title: Positive matching decomposition conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles
statement:
Let $C_m$ and $C_n$ be cycles with $m,n\geq3$, and let $\mathrm{pmd}(G)$ denote the positive matching decomposition number. **Positive matching decomposition conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles.**

$$
\mathrm{pmd}(C_m\square C_n)=6
$$

for all $m,n\geq3$ such that $m+n$ is even, or such that $(m,n)\in\{(3,4),(3,6),(5,6)\}$. The supplied text presents this exact-value assertion after an analysis of positive matchings in the relevant Cartesian products; no resolution beyond that analysis is provided.
source_name: Mohammad Farrokhi Derakhshandeh Ghouchan and Ali Akbar Yazdan Pour, “Positive matching decompositions of the cartesian product of graphs”, arXiv:2502.02826 (2025).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2405.20480](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20480), [arXiv:2202.10463](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.10463).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02826

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).

title: The neighborhood-tour conjecture for ASEP vertices
statement: Let $P_{\text{ASEP}}^{n}$ be the asymmetric subtour elimination polytope, let $\boldsymbol{x}$ be a vertex of this polytope, and let $\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{x})$ denote its neighborhood in the vertex structure considered by the paper. A **tour** is a Hamiltonian cycle of the complete directed graph on the node set. **Neighborhood-tour conjecture.** For every vertex $\boldsymbol{x}$, the neighborhood $\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{x})$ contains at least one tour. This is presented as a conjecture based on preliminary computational tests; the supplied text does not establish it or indicate a resolution.
source_name: Eleonora Vercesi, Janos Barta, Luca Maria Gambardella, Stefano Gualandi and Monaldo Mastrolilli, “On the integrality Gap of Small Asymmetric Traveling Salesman Problems: A Polyhedral and Computational Approach”, arXiv:2506.10671 (2025).

title: The representation-number conjecture for larger toroidal grid graphs
statement:
Let $\text{TGr}_{m,n}$ be the toroidal grid graph formed from the Cartesian product of the cycle graphs $C_m$ and $C_n$, with $m,n\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ denote the representation number of a graph $G$. **Representation-number conjecture.** If $n,m\geq 3$ and $m+n\geq 8$, then

$$
\mathcal{R}(\text{TGr}_{m,n})\geq 4.
$$

The graphs $\text{TGr}_{3,3}$ and $\text{TGr}_{3,4}$ have known 3-representations, but no 3-representation is known for larger toroidal grid graphs; the conjecture predicts that all cases with $m+n\geq 8$ require representation number at least $4$.
source_name: Nawaf Shafi Alshammari, Sergey Kitaev and Artem Pyatkin, “On the representation number of grid graphs and cylindric grid graphs”, arXiv:2507.16469 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16469

title: Existence of regular open and closed XOR-magic graphs of power-of-two order
statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $d$ be a degree. An **open XOR-magic graph** and a **closed XOR-magic graph** are graphs admitting, respectively, an open or closed XOR-magic labeling. The graphs below are required to have order $2^n$.

For each degree

$$
d\in\{5,7,\ldots,2^n-7,2^n-5\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular open XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$. For each degree

$$
d\in\{4,6,\ldots,2^n-6,2^n-4\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular closed XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$.

**Existence conjecture.** For every permitted degree $d$ in the two displayed sets, the corresponding regular open or closed XOR-magic graph exists. This would complete the existence picture apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result and extend the constructions known for order $16$ and order $8$ to every order that is a power of two.
source_name: Sylwia Cichacz, Hubert Grochowski and Rita Zuazua, “Open XOR-magic odd graphs and closed XOR-magic even graphs”, arXiv:2512.19278 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19278

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

title: The collapsing conjecture for facets of hierarchical model polytopes
statement:
Let $p\leq q\leq r$ be positive integers, and let $P_\Delta^{p,q,r}$ denote the polytope associated with the hierarchical model in the paper. A facet is **obtained by collapsing** if it arises from a facet of a smaller table through the paper's collapsing operation.

**Collapsing conjecture.** Suppose that

$$
p \leq q \leq r.
$$

Then all facets of $P_\Delta^{p,q,r}$ are obtained by collapsing from facets of $P_\Delta^{p,q,q}$.

The conjecture is motivated by computational results summarized in the paper's table, although the authors also exhibit a non-collapsible facet of $P_\Delta^{4,4,4}$, showing that not every facet arises by collapsing to a binary table. The conjecture remains open in the supplied source.
source_name: Nicholas Eriksson, Stephen E. Fienberg, Alessandro Rinaldo and Seth Sullivant, “Polyhedral conditions for the nonexistence of the MLE for hierarchical log-linear models”, arXiv:math/0405044 (2004).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405044

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2004).

title: The distance bound for loops with nonequivalent associator
statement:
Let $L=(G,\circ)$ and $M=(G,*)$ be Moufang loops on the same set $G$ of order $n$, and define their distance by

$$
d(\circ,*)=\left|\{(a,b)\in G\times G: a\circ b\ne a*b\}\right|.
$$
 Suppose that $L$ and $M$ have nonequivalent associators. **Distance-bound conjecture.** Their distance satisfies

$$
d(\circ,*)\ge 3n^2/8.
$$
 This conjecture asks for the minimum distance between Moufang loops with nonequivalent associator; the source gives no evidence of a proof or disproof.
source_name: Aleš Drápal and Petr Vojtěchovský, “Moufang loops that share associator and three quarters of their multiplication tables”, arXiv:math/0701710 (2007).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701710

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).

title: Cardoso–Luz conjecture on adverse graphs
statement:
An **adverse graph** is a graph $H$ without isolated vertices such that $upsilon(H)$ and $lambda_{min}(H)$ are integers, and, for every vertex $i\in V(H)$,

$$
\upsilon(H-N_H(i))=\upsilon(H),\qquad \lambda_{min}(H-N_H(i))=\lambda_{min}(H).
$$

Here $upsilon(H)$ is the optimal value of the quadratic stability-number bound and $lambda_{min}(H)$ is the least eigenvalue of $H$. A graph is a **$\mathcal{Q}$-graph** when it belongs to the class $\mathcal{Q}$ defined in the paper.

**Cardoso–Luz conjecture.** All adverse graphs are $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.

Computational tests with adverse graphs supported the conjecture, but it remains open. Its resolution would clarify the polynomial-time recognition of $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.
source_name: Domingos M. Cardoso, “A survey on graphs with convex quadratic stability number”, arXiv:1811.05516 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.05516

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2018). “Notice that all performed computational tests with adverse graphs supported the validity of Conjecture , however the conjecture remains open.”

title: Conjecture on the super edge-magic total strength of odd-cycle unicyclic graphs
statement:
Let $G(n;k_{1},\dots,k_{n})$ be the super edge-magic total unicyclic $(p,q)$-graph consisting of an odd cycle

$$
C_n=\{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n\}
$$

and $k_i$ pendant vertices adjacent to each $a_i$, for $1\leq i\leq n$. Here $s m(G)$ denotes the super edge-magic total strength of $G$. **Super edge-magic total strength conjecture.**

$$
s m(G(n;k_{1},\dots,k_{n}))=2q+\frac{n+3}{2}.
$$

The claim extends the known exact value for the uniform family $k_i=k$, while the paper presents computations for certain graphs in this broader family as supporting evidence; its general validity remains open.
source_name: Nayana Shibu Deepthi, “Super edge-magic total strength of some unicyclic graphs”, arXiv:2212.05329 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.05329

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

title: Orientation of nonideal clutters
statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a clutter on ground set V, and let $\mathcal{B}$ be its blocker. Is it true that $\mathcal{C}$ is nonideal if and only if there exist $p:{\mathcal C} \to V$ and $q: {\mathcal B} \to V$ such that $p(X)\in X$ for every $X \in {\mathcal C}$, $p(Y)\in Y$ for every $Y \in {\mathcal B}$, if $p(X)=q(Y)$, then $|X \cap Y|>1$?
source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems
